claims.text: Inconel 718 or a comparable Ni-based superalloy can be used to study temperature-dependent plastic deformation from room temperature to about 700°C.
The yield strength of the proposed alloy will remain stable or increase slightly up to moderate temperatures.
The ductility of the proposed alloy will remain stable or increase slightly up to moderate temperatures.
Precipitation strengthening contributes to maintaining strength at lower and moderate temperatures.
Controlled dislocation motion contributes to the proposed stable or increasing strength and ductility at moderate temperatures.
Strength will decrease when the testing temperature exceeds approximately 650–700°C.
Ductility will decrease when the testing temperature exceeds approximately 650–700°C.
The proposed Inconel 718 microstructure contains γ′ and γ″ precipitates in a Ni-based matrix.
The γ′/γ″ precipitates coarsen as testing temperature increases.
The precipitate size and distribution influence dislocation dynamics.
At lower and moderate temperatures, precipitates inhibit dislocation motion and strengthen the alloy.
At higher temperatures, increased atomic diffusion facilitates dislocation activity.
Accelerated precipitate coarsening at high temperature eases dislocation activity and causes reduced strength.
The specimens will be solution-treated and then tested in an age-hardened condition.
Uniaxial tensile tests will be conducted at 25°C, 200°C, 400°C, 600°C, and 700°C at a constant or controlled strain rate.
Short-term dwell times of up to one hour are intended to isolate behavior at or below 700°C.
The onset temperature for declining strength and ductility depends on alloy composition and prior thermal history.
